publisher: Deloitte (Deloitte Consulting LLP, Office of the CTO)
title: Tech Trends 2026
notes: 'the 17th annual edition of Tech Trends'. 'For 17 years, Tech Trends has explored emerging technologies poised to reshape business in the next 18 to 24 months.' Five trend chapters (entries 1-5) and a closing chapter, 'Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances', with eight signals (entries 6-13). Deloitte on the signals: 'Signals aren’t predictions. They’re observations of forces already in motion'; they 'didn’t make the cut for full chapters'. Numbers in the signals section are third-party projections cited by Deloitte and are not recorded as values. The executive summary opens: 'Last year’s Tech Trends report predicted that artificial intelligence would become akin to electricity ... This year’s report ... proves that hypothesis.' The introduction ('Innovation compounds') is not a trend. published from the edition page (10 December 2025).

entries.label: AI goes physical: Navigating the convergence of AI and robotics
entries.quote: Over the coming 18 to 24 months, resolving these foundational issues will likely enable physical AI and robotics to expand beyond traditional industries.
entries.subject: Physical AI and robotics
entries.note: Same chapter: 'During the next decade, the intersection of agentic AI systems with physical AI robotic systems will result in robots whose “brains” are agentic AIs.' The executive summary cites 'projections of 2 million workplace humanoids by 2035' (a UBS estimate per the chapter, not Deloitte's own).

entries.label: The agentic reality check: Preparing for a silicon-based workforce
entries.quote: Leading organizations are adopting agent-first process redesign, implementing multiagent orchestration using emerging protocols, and treating agents as a silicon-based workforce requiring specialized management frameworks.
entries.subject: Agentic AI
entries.note: Executive summary quote. It also reports a Deloitte survey figure: 'Only 11% of surveyed organizations have deployed agentic systems in production' (a measurement, not a forecast).

entries.label: The AI infrastructure reckoning: Optimizing compute strategy in the age of inference economics
entries.quote: Leading enterprises are adopting strategic hybrid architectures: cloud for variable workloads, on-premises for consistent production inference, and edge for latency-critical applications.
entries.subject: AI infrastructure and inference compute
entries.note: Executive summary quote. Chapter: 'Over the next five to 20 years, as emerging computing paradigms mature, data centers will need to continue to evolve'.

entries.label: The great rebuild: Architecting an AI-native tech organization
entries.quote: Future tech organizations will feature agentic architectures, lean product-led teams, blended human-agent workforces, adaptive governance, and ecosystem-oriented innovation.
entries.subject: AI-native technology organization

entries.label: The AI dilemma: Securing and leveraging AI for cyber defense
entries.quote: AI creates a cybersecurity paradox: The same capabilities driving business innovation are also introducing new risks.
entries.subject: AI security and AI for cyber defense

entries.label: Are foundation models reaching a plateau?
entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: How well businesses deploy, fine-tune, and integrate AI into redesigned processes will likely matter more than having the latest foundation model.
entries.subject: Foundation model scaling
entries.note: Signal, not a full trend chapter; Deloitte: 'Signals aren’t predictions.'

entries.label: New data > synthetic data > old data.
entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: Those with access to fresh information—real-time user interactions, proprietary business data, breaking research— have the advantage.
entries.subject: Synthetic data for AI training
entries.note: Signal, not a full trend chapter; Deloitte: 'Signals aren’t predictions.' The section cites 'predictions that 80% of data used by AI tools will be synthetic by 2028' (third party, not recorded as a value).

entries.label: Neuromorphic chips supercharge computing.
entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: Widespread adoption of neuromorphic computing is expected by 2030.
entries.subject: Neuromorphic computing
entries.note: Signal, not a full trend chapter; Deloitte: 'Signals aren’t predictions.' The sentence carries a footnote to a third-party market report; Deloitte states it without naming the source in the text.

entries.label: The rise of edge AI and on-device processing.
entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: This is a fundamental shift already in motion.
entries.subject: Edge AI (on-device processing)
entries.note: Signal, not a full trend chapter; Deloitte: 'Signals aren’t predictions.' The section cites a third-party projection of 912 million generative-AI-capable smartphones by 2028 (not recorded as a value).

entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: The winning form factor—if one emerges at all—remains undetermined, with success dependent on addressing privacy concerns and delivering functionality that justifies carrying an additional device.
entries.subject: AI wearables and AI-native devices

entries.label: Biometric authentication as next-level cybersecurity.
entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: The future points toward hybrid approaches where biometrics serve as the primary but not exclusive verification method.
entries.subject: Biometric authentication

entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: Truly capable personal AI assistants require unprecedented access to personal data—and that access is already being granted.

entries.label: GEO overtakes SEO.
entries.section: Cutting through the noise: Tech signals worth tracking as AI advances
entries.quote: The race is on to appear in AI-generated answers— a shift from search engine optimization (SEO) to generative engine optimization (GEO).
entries.subject: Generative engine optimization (GEO)
entries.note: Signal, not a full trend chapter; Deloitte: 'Signals aren’t predictions.' The section cites a third-party projection that AI platforms' share of organic traffic will reach 14.5% within a year (not recorded as a value).
